# A template from registered to removed

Register it, mark it ready, create instances, retire it, remove it. Each state
is the operator's to control, and the product refuses steps taken out of order.

## Register

```bash
rimsky template register template.yml --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky template list --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky template get "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
```

Registration returns a content-addressed template id. The catalogue lists the
template in state `registered`, and `template get` returns the stored spec
unchanged.

## Mark it ready

```bash
rimsky instance create "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
# refused — the template is registered, not deployed

rimsky template deploy "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json

rimsky instance create "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
# accepted
```

Being in the catalogue and being runnable are separate states. A definition can
be registered and reviewed without anyone being able to start work from it yet.

## Retire it

While an instance is live:

```bash
rimsky template undeploy "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE"
# refused — "template has active instances"

rimsky template rm "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE"
# refused — "undeploy first"
```

Kill the instance, then retire:

```bash
rimsky instance kill "$IID" --force --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky template undeploy "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE"
```

The template moves to `undeployed`, and further `instance create` calls are
refused. New work stops starting without disturbing work already running.

## Remove it

```bash
rimsky template rm "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE"
# refused while a terminated instance's record still references the template

rimsky instance delete "$IID" --endpoint "$BASE" --yes
rimsky template rm "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE"
```

The catalogue no longer lists the template. The operator can only remove what
nothing points at.

That last refusal arrives as an HTTP 500 carrying the raw storage text
`FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, not as a conflict naming the referencing rows.
The operation is correctly refused; its diagnosis does not name the record
holding it. Delete the instance records first.
